advisories.what: Door beat (about 24.4 to 25.6 s): the vertical's baked headline THE DOOR IS OPEN (top) and the short's own caption 'the door is open' (bottom) are on screen together, so the same four words read twice for about 1.2 s. Not overlapping, not cut, not a doubled caption track (span-03 source carries no burned caption there), just redundant.
advisories.fix: Optional: suppress that one caption group while the headline is up (the same treatment s_captions already gives the other burned-text windows), letting 'you already / have the / skills.' carry on. Or keep as is; Mike's call.

advisories.what: Seam 1 whip (frames 250 to 252): 'my god, dude' pops in while the 2x whip-blurred chart labels (MEDIAN / TOP 10% / DATA POINTS rows) are still settling and briefly touch the caption top. 3 frames of motion blur, not visible at speed; from frame 253 the caption sits clear below the labels.
advisories.fix: None needed. If ever re-cut: start the caption group 3 frames later.

advisories.what: Frame 0 is the vertical's baked F1 mirror-tile open (mirrored copies of Mike's face). Intended effect, resolves by frame 3; only matters if a platform auto-picks frame 0 as the cover.
advisories.fix: Pick a clean face frame (e.g. 1.0 s) as the cover where the platform allows.

advisories.what: C3 chart footer reads 'LEVELS.FYI . UNITED STATES . TOTAL COMP . READ 2026-11-09 .' with a dangling trailing separator. Inherited from the vertical / longform chart asset (present in span-02 source), not introduced by the short; sits well inside the frame.
advisories.fix: None for the short; fix in the chart source if the chart is ever rebuilt.

advisories.what: The final-sheet-0N.jpg time labels run about 0.2 s BEHIND the real frame times (sheet '8.000' = frame 247 / 8.233 s seam-1 whip; sheet '20.000' = frames 605-608 / 20.17 s seam-2 whip; sheet '27.000' = outro fully up, frame 815+). All timestamps in this report are real frame times from ffmpeg frame-exact extraction.
advisories.fix: s_qa_final contact-sheet sampler: select by frame number (n mod 15) and label from n/fps.
